messages:
marta: quick check — when a process wants to shut down and we have an active streaming call (client.streamChat / streaming embeddings), what are the expected semantics across SDKs? do we prefer to wait for in-flight tokens to finish, or abort immediately and let callers retry? any standard AbortController/context patterns we should recommend? :thinking:

ryan: short answer: prefer cooperative cancellation via AbortController (or equivalent). Node SDK accepts a signal param on streaming calls and will close the stream cleanly when aborted. example:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const stream = client.chat.stream({ messages, signal: ac.signal });
// later, to cancel:
ac.abort();
```

ryan: note: aborting stops the client from emitting more tokens, but the server may have already started compute for a chunk of tokens — that work can be billed. clients should trim retries after an abort to avoid double-sends.

samir: runtime/serving note — when a client cancels we treat it as a client-cancel; we try to unwind decoding loops and free kernels, but some queued work may still finish on the GPU. semantics: best-effort fast stop, not guaranteed rollback.

alex: Python side is similar — we have a signal shim that maps to asyncio CancelledError. example usage (py pseudocode):

```py
ac = AbortController()  # py shim in SDK
stream = client.chat.stream(..., signal=ac.signal)
ac.abort()
```

alex: also recommend using short client-side idle timeouts for streams (keeps lambda/container sockets from lingering).

marta: for background workers that are SIGTERMing, what's a recommended unwind pattern? try to finish one token then exit? drain loop for X ms?

ryan: common pattern we ship in examples: on SIGTERM set abort, then wait up to 500ms for stream to flush client-side buffers, then force close. that avoids blocking shutdown forever but gives short completion window. for critical requests, use explicit ack at app layer.

samir: and on the server we have a graceful-unwind window for Dedicated deployments (configurable). outside that, network-level aborts are final. also note: retries should include idempotency tokens to avoid duplicate side effects.

alex: I hit a flaky test in CI where the SDK stream didn't close after abort (test times out). log snippet: 

ci-bot: build 4821 failed: sdk-shutdown-suite::test_stream_abort — AssertionError: stream still open after abort (timeout waiting 2s)

marta: thanks — can someone own a tiny ecosystem fix: helper that ensures stream.close() on abort and an e2e that simulates SIGTERM? also add docs showing the recommended signal + timeout pattern.

ryan: I can PR a small helper in node-sdk: `withAbortTimeout(streamPromise, signal, graceMs)` that calls abort, waits graceMs, then force-closes. will add unit + a tiny e2e that spawns a child and SIGTERM.

samir: i'll add a server note about billing and partial-token accounting in runtime docs so customers know abort isn't free.

alex: for Python I'll add an example using contextlib.AsyncExitStack to ensure stream is closed in handler and update the CI test to be less timing-sensitive.

marta: perfect. let's also add one line to the migration guide: "AbortController semantics: cooperative cancelation; client may still be billed for in-flight tokens; use idempotency for retries and small grace windows for shutdown."

ryan: will follow up with PR link when ready, ping me for review.

marta: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
